newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends mostly firmer, but rangebound.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends mostly firmer, but rangebound.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended mostly firmer but rangebound at the close on Tuesday, showing little response to a U.S. stock drawdown and strong Brazilian exports, traders said.
Rio de Janeiro Coffee Center said on Tuesday the country's exports for October already totalled 1.70 million 60-kg bags based on bills of lading.
Brazilian exporters said the final October figure would certainly be higher than 1.7 million bags.
"I don't think there's any market reaction to the news," said a trader. "Everybody expects it anyway...that's the possible number that would be achieved."
By the close, most-active January was $12 up at $1,401 a tonne after a high of $1,402 but front-month November was $14 down at $1,495.
LIFFE said on Tuesday that a further 231 originals and one retender were posted against the spot November contract, bringing the total tenders to 293 lots of which one was a retender.
Traders expect the large November premium against the back month January to narrow further as sellers put up their coffee for tender to take advantage of the premium.
The Nov/Jan spread stood at $94 at the close, down from Monday's finish of $125.
News of the latest draw in U.S. exchange-certified stocks also failed to drum up interest from London and New York, traders said.
"What is the difference between 1,500 bags and 800 bags?" asked one trader. "It doesn't mean anything, does it?"
Others agreed that news of a fresh fall in the U.S. certified stocks by 743 60-kg bags to 804 bags had been psychologically factored into the market.
Traders said the New York arabica market, now in neutral territory, could provide a fresh stimulus to London if it breaks the immediate range of 112 and 123 cents a lb basis December.
"117 on Dec is a neutral territory...Really to set the fireworks alight, it's got to get above 123 or go below 112," one said.
